userStories.title: Node glob lists files under a literal .nax prefix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make Node async and sync agent Glob discover visible files under an explicitly named leading .nax directory without exposing other hidden paths.

**Motivation** — nax's own artifacts (briefs, reports, the ledger) live under `.nax/`, so an agent can Read them but never find them.

**Approach** — Glob `.nax` exemption (both runtimes), Node portion verbatim:
- Rule: strip leading `./` segments from the pattern. If its first `/`-separated segment is exactly `.nax` (no glob metacharacter, no escape), a result whose **first** result-relative segment is `.nax` is not hidden for that segment. Every other dot segment in the result, including deeper ones under `.nax/`, is still hidden, and a pattern whose first segment is anything else (`**`, `.nax-wt`, `{.nax,src}`) hides `.nax/` as today.
- `nodeGlob` / `nodeGlobSync` (`nax-agent/src/runtime/node-glob.ts`): `scanOptions`' `exclude` and `filePath`'s result filter both apply the rule, so Node descends into `.nax` only for an exempt pattern.
- The shared `GLOB_CASES` contract (`packages/test-kit/src/cases/glob-cases.ts`) is unchanged and still passes: none of its patterns starts with `.nax`.

**Scope** — In: packages/nax-agent/src/runtime/node-glob.ts and new packages/nax-agent/test/unit/runtime/node-glob-nax-dir.test.ts. Out: Bun runtime changes belong to US-002; workflow orchestration/config/prompts belong to US-003–US-009. Glob exposure of any dot path other than a literal leading `.nax` segment: ruling D21 stands for `.git`, `.env`, `.nax-wt` and every other hidden path. ACP agents' own Glob tools, which nax does not implement. Adding the `.nax` exemption cases to the shared `GLOB_CASES` contract in `packages/test-kit`: each runtime pins them in its own test file.

**Interface** — Existing runtime entry points remain unchanged: `nodeGlob` / `nodeGlobSync`; `scanOptions` and `filePath` implement the exemption. All ACs use a temporary root holding `.nax/features/f/workflow/r1/US-001/report.md`, `.nax/.hidden/x.md`, `.nax-wt/a.ts`, `.git/HEAD` and `src/a.ts`. Reuse the shared fixture/testing conventions; preserve relative leading ./ output and absolute output behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob(".nax/features/**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields exactly .nax/features/f/workflow/r1/US-001/report.md.
AC-2 [unit] nodeRuntime.globSync(".nax/features/**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields exactly .nax/features/f/workflow/r1/US-001/report.md.
AC-3 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob("./.nax/features/**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields exactly ./.nax/features/f/workflow/r1/US-001/report.md.
AC-4 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob(".nax/**/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields the report path and not .nax/.hidden/x.md, because a dot segment below .nax stays hidden.
AC-5 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob("**/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields exactly src/a.ts, so a wildcard first segment never reaches .nax/.
AC-6 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob("**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields nothing.
AC-7 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob(".nax-wt/**/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields nothing.
AC-8 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob("{.nax,src}/**/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields exactly src/a.ts.
AC-9 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob(".git/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields nothing.
AC-10 [unit] nodeRuntime.glob(".nax/features/**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: true }) yields exactly the absolute path of the report under root.

routing.reasoning: Two existing hidden-result filters must agree with Node scan pruning; focused TDD covers this bounded listing change without altering read permissions or session management.

suggestedCriteria: nodeRuntime.glob("././.nax/features/**/report.md", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) yields the report path with both leading ./ segments preserved.
nodeRuntime.glob with an escaped first segment spelling .nax yields no hidden report paths.
nodeRuntime.globSync(".nax/**/*", { cwd: root, absolute: false }) excludes .nax/.hidden/x.md.

userStories.title: Add interrupt retry configuration and continue/report prompts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Define workflow interrupt/report budgets and the exact warm-session prompts consumed by later stories.

**Motivation** — No nax code checks `report.md` before review; the story reviewer discovers its absence, which costs a spec fail and a fix round.

**Approach** — Config (`src/config/schemas-workflow.ts`), verbatim:
- `workflow.interruptRetry`: `{ maxAttempts: int >= 0, default 1; budgetMultiplier: number > 0 and <= 1, default 0.5 }`, a nested object with `.prefault({})`. `maxAttempts: 0` turns the continue off.
- `workflow.timeouts.reportMs`: positive int, default `600_000` (10 minutes).
- `WorkflowConfig` (`src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts`) gains the matching fields; `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` (`src/cli/config-descriptions.ts`) gains `workflow.interruptRetry`, `workflow.interruptRetry.maxAttempts`, `workflow.interruptRetry.budgetMultiplier` and `workflow.timeouts.reportMs`. `docs/guides/workflow-mode.md` (config table plus a short "Step limits" paragraph) and `docs/guides/configuration.md` document them.

Prompts (`src/prompts/builders/workflow-implementer-builder.ts`, exported through `src/prompts/index.ts`), verbatim:
- `buildWorkflowContinuePrompt(input: { storyId: string; reportPath: string; limitMinutes: number; budgetMinutes: number; attempt: number; maxAttempts: number; changedFiles?: readonly string[] }): string`. Text, in order:
  - `You were stopped at the <limitMinutes>-minute step limit before you finished story <storyId>. This is continue attempt <attempt> of <maxAttempts>; you have up to <budgetMinutes> minutes.`
  - the changed files: `Files changed since the story base:` and one `- <path>` line each; or `No files have changed since the story base.` for `[]`; or `The changed-file list could not be read; check git status yourself.` when `changedFiles` is undefined;
  - `Continue from where you stopped. Do not revert, delete or redo work that is already on disk.`
  - `When you are done, commit your work, write <reportPath>, and end your reply with the json status block. If you cannot finish in this turn, commit what you have, write the report marking each unfinished acceptance criterion, and reply DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.`
  - `WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT`, last.
  It does not resend the brief: the warm session already holds it.
- `buildWorkflowReportPrompt(input: { storyId: string; reportPath: string }): string`. Text: `Your report for story <storyId> is missing: <reportPath> does not exist. Write it now for the work you already did, with the sections the implement prompt listed: What was built, TDD evidence, Files changed, Decisions & assumptions. Report only evidence you captured; for an acceptance criterion whose failing run you did not capture, say so under Decisions & assumptions. Do not change any other file.` then `WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_RULE` and `WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT`, last.

**Scope** — In: schema, WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS, runtime types, CLI descriptions, root guides, implementer builders and public prompts barrel. Out: turn execution belongs to US-004, real env wiring to US-005, retry/fallback orchestration to US-006/US-007, report checks to US-008, branch listing to US-009.

**Interface** — Verbatim signatures:
```typescript
buildWorkflowContinuePrompt(input: { storyId: string; reportPath: string; limitMinutes: number; budgetMinutes: number; attempt: number; maxAttempts: number; changedFiles?: readonly string[] }): string
buildWorkflowReportPrompt(input: { storyId: string; reportPath: string }): string
```

Extend existing builder tests rather than inventing a new test-only story. Guide paths are repository-root relative even though the binding workdir is packages/nax.

userStories.title: Execute continue and report turns on the warm implementer session
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add continue/report turn kinds, budgets, model-preserving prompts and labels, and a best-effort auto-commit helper.

**Motivation** — Nothing tells the still-warm session it was cut off.

**Approach** — Turns (`src/workflow/implement.ts`), verbatim except the superseded zero-minute budget expression is resolved to the final at-least-one-minute ruling:
- `ImplementTurn` gains two kinds:
  - `{ kind: "continue"; limit: "implement" | "fix"; stepUps: number; attempt: number; maxAttempts: number; changedFiles?: readonly string[] }`;
  - `{ kind: "report"; stepUps: number }`.
- `runImplementerTurn` timeouts: `continue` = `Math.floor(limitMs * workflow.interruptRetry.budgetMultiplier)`, where `limitMs` is `timeouts.implementMs` for `limit: "implement"` and `timeouts.fixMs` for `limit: "fix"`; `report` = `timeouts.reportMs`. Neither kind closes the session first (`closesSessionFirst` stays false for them). Both run on `implementerModelFor(sc, turn)`, so a continue keeps its origin's step-up.
- `promptFor`: `continue` renders `buildWorkflowContinuePrompt` with `limitMinutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(limitMs / 60_000))`, `budgetMinutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(continueTimeoutMs / 60_000))` and the turn's fields; `report` renders `buildWorkflowReportPrompt`.
- An interrupted turn of any kind still returns without auto-committing (unchanged).
- New export `autoCommitTurnEdits(sc: StepContext): Promise<boolean>`: reads the dirty list through the existing fail-open `dirtyAfterTurn` and, when it is non-empty, calls `_workflowDeps.autoCommitIfDirty(sc.projectDir, "workflow", "wf-implementer", sc.story.id, undefined, sc.dryRun)` and returns `true`; otherwise `false`. A throw from `autoCommitIfDirty` is caught, logged with `getSafeLogger()?.warn("workflow", "<message>", { storyId: sc.story.id, error: errorMessage(err) })` (`check:logger-storyid` requires the `storyId`), and returns `false`. `runImplementerTurn`'s own auto-commit goes through it.
- `budgetMinutes` in the continue prompt is at least 1 (`Math.max(1, Math.round(continueTimeoutMs / 60_000))`).

Label design, verbatim: `turnLabel` (`src/workflow/story-steps.ts`; `story-loop.ts` only re-exports it): `continue` -> `"implementer continue"`, `report` -> `"implementer report"`.

**Scope** — In: implement.ts union, prompt/timeout dispatch, model/session behavior, autoCommitTurnEdits, and story-steps turnLabel. Out: config/builders are US-003; step/env wiring is US-005; retry orchestration is US-006; fallback invocation/concern is US-007; report-check eligibility/state is US-008. Pipeline mode's interrupt and timeout handling, including `agent.timeoutRetry`: pipeline mode is frozen. Changing `STEP_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_MS` or the soft-interrupt mechanism in `softInterruptTurn`. A fresh-session retry or a restart of the story on a step-limit interrupt.

**Interface** — Verbatim target declarations:
```typescript
{ kind: "continue"; limit: "implement" | "fix"; stepUps: number; attempt: number; maxAttempts: number; changedFiles?: readonly string[] }
{ kind: "report"; stepUps: number }
autoCommitTurnEdits(sc: StepContext): Promise<boolean>
runImplementerTurn(sc, turn): Promise<ImplementOutcome>
```

Use the existing _workflowDeps.callOp seam and fakeImplement/makeStepContext tests. Preserve runSignal abort rethrow and failure handling. A report call still uses workflowImplementOp and its existing writableOutput reportPath; this story does not add tools or permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] runImplementerTurn with turn { kind: "continue", limit: "implement", stepUps: 0, attempt: 1, maxAttempts: 1 }, timeouts.implementMs 3600000 and interruptRetry.budgetMultiplier 0.5 passes timeoutMs: 1800000 to workflowImplementOp through _workflowDeps.callOp.
AC-2 [unit] runImplementerTurn with a continue turn of limit: "fix", timeouts.fixMs 1000001 and budgetMultiplier 0.5 passes timeoutMs: 500000.
AC-3 [unit] runImplementerTurn with a continue turn never calls closeImplementerSession (the session manager's close is not invoked).

AC-4 [unit] runImplementerTurn with turn { kind: "continue", limit: "implement", stepUps: 0, attempt: 1, maxAttempts: 1, changedFiles: ["src/a.ts"] }, implementMs 3600000 and multiplier 0.5 passes as prompt exactly buildWorkflowContinuePrompt({ storyId, reportPath, limitMinutes: 60, budgetMinutes: 30, attempt: 1, maxAttempts: 1, changedFiles: ["src/a.ts"] }).

AC-5 [unit] With a step context whose tierOrder holds two tiers, implementerModelFor for a continue turn with stepUps: 1 returns a defined model equal to the one it returns for a fix turn with stepUps: 1.
AC-6 [unit] runImplementerTurn with turn { kind: "report", stepUps: 0 } and timeouts.reportMs 600000 passes timeoutMs: 600000.
AC-7 [unit] runImplementerTurn with a report turn passes as prompt exactly buildWorkflowReportPrompt({ storyId, reportPath }).
AC-8 [unit] runImplementerTurn with a report turn never calls closeImplementerSession.
AC-9 [unit] An interrupted reply (interrupted: true) to a continue turn returns autoCommitted: false without calling autoCommitIfDirty.
AC-10 [unit] autoCommitTurnEdits(sc) with a dirty tree calls _workflowDeps.autoCommitIfDirty with (sc.projectDir, "workflow", "wf-implementer", sc.story.id, undefined, sc.dryRun).
AC-11 [unit] autoCommitTurnEdits(sc) with a dirty tree resolves true.
AC-12 [unit] autoCommitTurnEdits(sc) with a clean tree resolves false without calling autoCommitIfDirty.
AC-13 [unit] autoCommitTurnEdits(sc) when git status exits non-zero resolves false without calling autoCommitIfDirty.
AC-14 [unit] autoCommitTurnEdits(sc) with a dirty tree and autoCommitIfDirty rejecting resolves false.
AC-15 [unit] turnLabel returns "implementer continue" for a continue turn.
AC-16 [unit] turnLabel returns "implementer report" for a report turn.

Regression [unit] runImplementerTurn(sc, { kind: 'implement' }) with a non-interrupted DONE reply, a dirty tree and a successful auto-commit returns { reply, autoCommitted: true }, preserving the normal completed-turn auto-commit behavior through autoCommitTurnEdits.

routing.reasoning: Extends a discriminated turn executor using established seams; strict isolation is required because warm-session lifecycle and model preservation are involved.

suggestedCriteria: runImplementerTurn with a continue timeout below 30000 ms sends a prompt whose budget is at least 1 minute.

runImplementerTurn returns autoCommitted: false rather than rejecting when the completed turn's best-effort auto-commit rejects.

userStories.title: Wire story-loop interrupt and report evidence steps
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Supply the story loop with changed-file evidence, best-effort commit, report existence and configured interrupt limits.

**Motivation** — The implementer ran 60 minutes, the review diff showed no commits, review failed on `report.md` ENOENT, and fix round 1 spent 6 minutes committing the work and reconstructing the TDD evidence.

**Approach** — Steps and wiring (`src/workflow/story-loop.ts`, `src/workflow/stage-env.ts`, `src/workflow/no-work.ts`), relevant design verbatim:
- `StoryLoopSteps` gains three optional steps, each absent in a caller that has not wired it:
  - `workSinceBase?(): Promise<string[]>`: the files changed since the story base, committed or not;
  - `autoCommitDirty?(): Promise<boolean>`: the fallback auto-commit;
  - `reportExists?(): Promise<boolean>`: whether the story's `report.md` exists.
- `StoryLoopEnv` gains `readonly interrupt?: { readonly maxAttempts: number; readonly implementMs: number; readonly fixMs: number }`. Absent reads as `WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS` (`maxAttempts` 1, both limits 3,600,000).
- `no-work.ts` exports `storyChangedFiles(sc: StepContext): Promise<string[]>`: the union of `changedFilesSince(sc.projectDir, sc.base)` and `listUncommitted(sc.projectDir)`, deduplicated, in that order, with nax-owned paths (`isNaxOwned`) removed. It throws on a git error, like `storyWorkEvidence`.
- `buildStoryEnv` wires `workSinceBase: () => storyChangedFiles(sc)`, `autoCommitDirty: () => autoCommitTurnEdits(sc)`, `reportExists: () => Bun.file(sc.reportPath).exists()`, and `interrupt` from `workflow.interruptRetry.maxAttempts`, `workflow.timeouts.implementMs` and `workflow.timeouts.fixMs`.

**Scope** — In: optional step/env contracts, storyChangedFiles, real buildStoryEnv wiring and preservation of the existing workProduced evidence check. Out: turn labels/execution/helper implementation are US-004; changed-file check interpretation, retries and fallback are US-006/US-007; report-check interpretation and eligibility/state machine are US-008. Do not convert throwing git evidence reads into silent empty lists in storyChangedFiles.

**Interface** — Verbatim declarations:
```typescript
workSinceBase?(): Promise<string[]>
autoCommitDirty?(): Promise<boolean>
reportExists?(): Promise<boolean>
readonly interrupt?: { readonly maxAttempts: number; readonly implementMs: number; readonly fixMs: number }
storyChangedFiles(sc: StepContext): Promise<string[]>
```

Retain old callers without the optional steps. Tests should drive real buildStoryEnv using temporary report files and the existing _workflowDeps.git/autoCommitIfDirty seams, asserting the producer-consumer connections rather than interface existence.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] storyChangedFiles(sc) with git diff --name-only returning src/a.ts and .nax/features/f/x.md, and git status --porcelain returning ' M src/a.ts' and '?? src/b.ts', resolves ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"].
AC-2 [unit] storyChangedFiles(sc) rejects when git diff exits non-zero.

AC-3 [unit] buildStoryEnv with workflow.interruptRetry.maxAttempts: 2, timeouts.implementMs: 5400000 and timeouts.fixMs: 3600000 returns an env whose interrupt is { maxAttempts: 2, implementMs: 5400000, fixMs: 3600000 }.
AC-4 [unit] The env from buildStoryEnv has steps.reportExists resolving false while the story's report.md is absent, and true once that file is written.

AC-5 [unit] The env from buildStoryEnv, with _workflowDeps.git answering git diff --name-only with src/a.ts and git status --porcelain with '?? src/b.ts', has steps.workSinceBase() resolving ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"].
AC-6 [unit] The env from buildStoryEnv, with git status --porcelain answering ' M src/a.ts', has steps.autoCommitDirty() resolving true after calling _workflowDeps.autoCommitIfDirty once.

Regression [unit] The env from buildStoryEnv still has steps.workProduced() resolving true when git diff and git status return no visible files but sc.reportPath exists, preserving the existing report-as-work evidence check alongside the new optional steps.

routing.reasoning: Three optional I/O seams and stable git-file union are wired into the existing environment; temporary-file and injected-git TDD verifies them without changing session lifecycle.

userStories.title: Continue interrupted implementer turns before evaluating the story
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recover interrupted implement/restart/advisor-answer/fix outcomes on the same warm session within one shared per-absorption retry allowance.

**Motivation** — Nothing tells the still-warm session it was cut off.

**Approach** — Continue on interrupt (new `src/workflow/interrupt-continue.ts`, called from `absorbTurn`), retry/orchestration design verbatim:
- Signature: `continueAfterInterrupt(env: StoryLoopEnv, outcome: ImplementOutcome, origin: { stepUps: number; limit: "implement" | "fix" }, used: number, runTurn: (turn: ImplementTurn) => Promise<ImplementOutcome>): Promise<{ outcome: ImplementOutcome; used: number; fallback: boolean }>`. It is pure orchestration over `env`, like the rest of the loop, and is injected with `runTurn` to avoid an import cycle with `story-steps.ts` (the `runNoWorkLadder` pattern).
- `absorbTurn` hands every outcome to one helper in the same module, `absorbInterrupt(env, current, origin, used, runTurn): Promise<{ outcome: ImplementOutcome; used: number; fallback: boolean }>`, which calls `continueAfterInterrupt` only when the outcome has no `failure` and `reply.interrupted` is true and otherwise returns the outcome unchanged. It runs before the auto-commit note and the advisor-answer check, and `absorbTurn` keeps `used` across its whole call. `absorbTurn` scores 18 against `check:complexity`'s limit of 20 today, so its loop body gains no new branch: the interrupt test lives in `absorbInterrupt`, and setting `lastTurn` (US-008) goes through a small helper too. So the tries are counted per absorbed turn: the first implement turn (with its no-work restarts and answers) or one fix round.
- While `used < maxAttempts` and the outcome is interrupted:
  - cost limit reached (`env.steps.costExceeded()`): ledger note `implementer interrupted at the step limit (<limitMinutes> min): continue skipped, cost limit reached`, and stop trying;
  - otherwise: ledger note `implementer interrupted at the step limit (<limitMinutes> min): continuing on the warm session (attempt <n> of <maxAttempts>)`; read `changedFiles` from `env.steps.workSinceBase` (absent or throwing -> `undefined`); run `{ kind: "continue", limit: origin.limit, stepUps: origin.stepUps, attempt: n, maxAttempts, changedFiles }`; `used += 1`.
  `limitMinutes` is `Math.max(1, Math.round(limitMs / 60_000))`, with `limitMs` from `env.interrupt` (`implementMs` for `origin.limit: "implement"`, `fixMs` for `"fix"`).
- The first outcome that is not interrupted (including a `failure`) goes back to `absorbTurn` and is absorbed exactly as today: a DONE reply records no concern; NEEDS_CONTEXT or BLOCKED gets an advisor answer; a failure records `implementer session failed: <failure>`.
- A recovered interrupt writes only the "continuing" note: no concern and no `(interrupted)` line.

Out: US-007 adds the fallback auto-commit/note/replacement concern; until that dependent story the still-interrupted exhausted outcome is recorded through the existing concern flow, with fallback true available for the later state consumer. US-008 adds lastTurn/report state and report turns. A fresh-session retry or a restart of the story on a step-limit interrupt. absorbInterrupt(env, current, origin, used, runTurn): Promise<{ outcome: ImplementOutcome; used: number; fallback: boolean }>

Real operation throws are converted to failure by runImplementerTurn and must reach ordinary session-finding absorption, never fallback. Reuse shared loop helpers instead of duplicating a harness.

userStories.title: Auto-commit interrupt fallback and disclose unfinished work to story review
userStories.description:
**Goal** — After continue attempts are exhausted or cost-skipped, commit dirty edits best-effort and replace the interrupted concern with an accurate reviewer warning.

**Motivation** — The review diff showed no commits, review failed on `report.md` ENOENT, and fix round 1 spent 6 minutes committing the work and reconstructing the TDD evidence.

**Approach** — Fallback portion of Continue on interrupt, verbatim:
- **Fallback**, when the outcome is still interrupted after the loop: call `env.steps.autoCommitDirty` (absent -> skipped, read as `false`); when it returns `true`, ledger note `auto-committed the implementer's uncommitted edits`. The outcome goes back with its reply's `concerns` replaced (a spread, not a mutation) and `fallback: true`. The concern is `stopped at the step limit after <used> continue attempt(s); its uncommitted edits were auto-committed, and it may not have finished the story or written report.md` when the auto-commit returned `true`, and `stopped at the step limit after <used> continue attempt(s); nothing was auto-committed, and it may not have finished the story or written report.md` otherwise. `absorbTurn` then records it through the existing `recordConcern`, so the story reviewer's concerns and the ledger line `implementer (interrupted) DONE_WITH_CONCERNS: <that text>` both carry it.
- A recovered interrupt writes only the "continuing" note: no concern and no `(interrupted)` line.

Failure handling, verbatim:
- A continue turn fails (op throws or returns `failure`): Absorbed like any failed implementer turn: `implementer session failed: <failure>`; no fallback auto-commit.
- The cost limit is reached at an interrupt: No continue turn; the "continue skipped" note; then the fallback.
- `autoCommitDirty` reads no dirty file, cannot read the tree, its commit throws, or it is not wired: No auto-commit note; the fallback concern is still recorded, with the "nothing was auto-committed" wording.

**Scope** — In: add fallback behavior to interrupt-continue.ts from US-006 and fallback cases to its existing test file; update the interrupted-restart regression in story-loop-no-work.test.ts. Out: retry scheduling/accounting is US-006; best-effort commit helper and its exception containment are US-004; state/report-check suppression from fallback is US-008. Telling the re-review about an interrupt fallback in a fix round: the re-review prompt is unchanged. Rewriting or filtering existing ledger lines or deferred minors: a stale missing-report claim is settled in the branch-review prompt.

**Interface** — Existing US-006 contract, verbatim:
```typescript
continueAfterInterrupt(env: StoryLoopEnv, outcome: ImplementOutcome, origin: { stepUps: number; limit: "implement" | "fix" }, used: number, runTurn: (turn: ImplementTurn) => Promise<ImplementOutcome>): Promise<{ outcome: ImplementOutcome; used: number; fallback: boolean }>
```

The real autoCommitDirty seam is autoCommitTurnEdits, which resolves false on read/commit failures. Preserve the original reply object by spreading. Avoid duplicate auto-commit notes: fallback's note is distinct from completed-turn autoCommitted absorption. Update the existing "AC-21: an interrupted restart ends the ladder and the gates run on the concern" regression: turns after the warm restart include exactly one continue, gates run after it, and the review concern contains `stopped at the step limit after 1 continue attempt(s)` instead of the old `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS: step time limit reached`.

Every AC drives `runStoryLoop` with faked `StoryLoopSteps` whose `implement` returns scripted outcomes; "interrupted" means a reply `{ status: "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS", concerns: "step time limit reached", interrupted: true }`; `env.interrupt` is `{ maxAttempts: 1, implementMs: 3600000, fixMs: 3600000 }` unless an AC says otherwise.

userStories.title: Check and repair a missing story report before review
userStories.description:
**Goal** — On every eligible green-gate evaluate pass, request a missing report once from the same warm implementer session before story review or re-review.

**Motivation** — No nax code checks `report.md` before review; the story reviewer discovers its absence, which costs a spec fail and a fix round.

**Approach** — Report check (new `src/workflow/report-check.ts`, called from `evaluate`), verbatim:
- `StoryLoopState` gains `reportTurnRan: boolean` (initial `false`) and `lastTurn?: { status: ImplementerStatus; fallback: boolean; stepUps: number }` (initial `undefined`; a resumed story starts without one). The `LoopState` class (`story-steps.ts`) gains both fields and copies them in its constructor; `initialStoryState` sets them.
- `absorbTurn` sets `lastTurn` from the reply it finally absorbs, with the `stepUps` of the turn that produced it (`origin.stepUps`). When it returns early on a `failure` or with no reply, it clears `lastTurn` to `undefined`.
- `implementStep` and `fixStep` return `lastTurn` in their patches; `evaluateStep` returns `reportTurnRan`. The step-graph engine refuses an undeclared patch key (`STEP_GRAPH_UNDECLARED_OUTPUT`, `src/step-graph/run.ts`), so `STORY_GRAPH` (`src/workflow/story-graph.ts`) adds `lastTurn` to the `implement` and `fix` nodes' `produces` and `reportTurnRan` to the `evaluate` node's.
- `report-check.ts` exports `runReportCheck(env: StoryLoopEnv, state: { reportTurnRan: boolean; lastTurn?: StoryLoopState["lastTurn"] }, runTurn: (turn: ImplementTurn) => Promise<ImplementOutcome>): Promise<boolean>`, which returns the new `reportTurnRan`. `runTurn` is injected (the `runNoWorkLadder` pattern) to avoid an import cycle with `story-steps.ts`.
- In `evaluate`, after the gates come back not red and before `review`, nax runs the report turn when all of these hold:
  - `reportTurnRan` is false (at most one report turn per story);
  - `lastTurn` is set, its `status` is `DONE` or `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`, and `fallback` is false;
  - `env.steps.costExceeded()` is false;
  - `env.steps.reportExists` is wired and resolves `false` (a throw reads as present, so no turn).
- The turn: ledger note `report.md missing after the implementer's reply: asking the session to write it`; run `{ kind: "report", stepUps: lastTurn.stepUps }` through the labelled turn runner, so it runs on the same model, and so the same warm session, as the turn that replied; set `reportTurnRan`. Its outcome is **not** absorbed (no concern, no advisor answer, no session finding). Afterwards, one ledger note: `report turn failed: <failure>` on a failure; else `report turn: report written` when `reportExists` now resolves `true`; else `report turn: report still missing, reviewing without it`. An interrupted report turn gets no continue. Review then runs as today.

Absorption complexity note, verbatim: `absorbTurn` scores 18 against `check:complexity`'s limit of 20 today, so its loop body gains no new branch: the interrupt test lives in `absorbInterrupt`, and setting `lastTurn` (US-008) goes through a small helper too.

**Scope** — In: new report-check.ts/test, StoryLoopState and LoopState fields, final absorbed-turn bookkeeping, graph output declarations, evaluate ordering and existing test fixture corrections. Out: retry/fallback execution is US-006/US-007; continue/report prompts and turn execution are US-003/US-004; real reportExists wiring is US-005; branch report listing is US-009. A report turn for a resumed story before any implementer turn has run in this process. Continue turns for the branch fix, the branch review, the story review or the re-review: only story implementer turns (implement, restart, answer, fix round) continue.

**Interface** — Verbatim declarations:
```typescript
reportTurnRan: boolean
lastTurn?: { status: ImplementerStatus; fallback: boolean; stepUps: number }
runReportCheck(env: StoryLoopEnv, state: { reportTurnRan: boolean; lastTurn?: StoryLoopState["lastTurn"] }, runTurn: (turn: ImplementTurn) => Promise<ImplementOutcome>): Promise<boolean>
```

Test setup for numbered ACs: drive runStoryLoop with gates green, storyReview recording call order, costExceeded false, and scripted reportExists unless an AC overrides them. Update packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/story-graph.test.ts EXPECTED_PRODUCES exactly: implement/fix gain lastTurn, evaluate gains reportTurnRan, maintaining equality to the keys each patch can carry. Update packages/nax/test/integration/workflow/story-e2e.test.ts fakeAgent and packages/nax/test/integration/workflow/advisor-e2e.test.ts fakeWorkflowAgent so every workflowImplementOp branch writes input.reportPath. The invariant is that a story whose implementer writes its report sends no report turn, preserving the existing two operation calls and two advisor-flow prompts rather than loosening their counts. Report outcomes must not overwrite lastTurn or enter ordinary absorption. A failure or missing reply from a later fix clears stale prior DONE state, suppressing repair. Existence checks fail open as present, including checks after a report turn.

userStories.title: List authoritative story report paths in branch review
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give branch review a present/missing report inventory and instructions to leave stale report-absence claims when the listed report exists.

**Motivation** — The branch reviewer cannot find the reports.

**Approach** — Story report listing (branch review), verbatim:
- `BranchReviewPromptInput` gains `storyReports?: readonly { storyId: string; path: string; present: boolean }[]`. When it is non-empty, `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` adds, right after `## Stories`, a `## Story reports` section: `- <storyId>: <path>` for a present report, `- <storyId>: no report (<path> does not exist)` for a missing one, then the line `A deferred minor or cannot-verify item that says a story's report is missing or unreadable is settled by this list: when the list shows the report, triage that minor "leave" and do not repeat the claim in "cannotVerify".`. Absent or empty: no section (the `nax bot review` prompt is unchanged).
- The `stories` entries of `BranchReviewPromptInput` gain `runDir?: string`. `reviewFacts` (`src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`) passes each `StorySummary.runDir` through. `feature-steps.ts` is at 597 of the 600 lines `check:file-sizes` allows, so this change must not grow it past 600: use the truthy one-line spread `...(s.runDir ? { runDir: s.runDir } : {})`, which fits Biome's 120-column width, not a `!== undefined` form that Biome wraps onto several lines.
- `runBranchReview` builds `storyReports` from `input.facts.stories`: each story with a `runDir` maps to `path = join(workflowStoryDir(runDir, id), "report.md")` and `present` from a new `_workflowDeps.fileExists(path)` (default `Bun.file(path).exists()`); a throw reads as present. Stories without `runDir` are not listed.

**Scope** — In: workflow-branch-builder.ts input/prompt, feature-steps.ts reviewFacts propagation, branch-review.ts report inventory and step-context.ts fileExists seam. Out: runtime Glob fixes are US-001/US-002, implementer retries/fallback and report repair are US-003–US-008. Rewriting or filtering existing ledger lines or deferred minors: a stale missing-report claim is settled in the branch-review prompt. A new `nax` subcommand or agent tool that lists story reports. Telling the re-review about an interrupt fallback in a fix round: the re-review prompt is unchanged.

**Interface** — Verbatim additions:
```typescript
storyReports?: readonly { storyId: string; path: string; present: boolean }[]
runDir?: string
fileExists(path: string): Promise<boolean>
```

Keep BranchReviewFacts structurally based on the existing prompt input and let runDir survive the feature-step boundary. Use the per-story runDir, not the current feature runDir, so reports from earlier runs remain readable. Extend existing branch-review and prompt tests using _workflowDeps.callOp capture and restore fileExists after each test. Omission is backwards compatible with nax bot review; no new public tool or command is introduced.
